## Purpose

Start a new question or update in an existing Discord conversation, even when
every earlier input has been answered. Use `aq supervisor-inbox say` with
`--conversation-id`, `--idempotency-key` and exactly one of `--text` or `--file`.

## When a playbook uses it

The live supervisor can use this for a worker's interview question or
clarification. Project supervisors can post to conversations addressed to their
project by the latest ordinary input; the live global supervisor and local
operator can also post. Workers and playbook principals cannot call it directly.

## How it works internally

[`conversation_commands.py`](../../../src/commands/conversation_commands.py)
checks the current supervisor launch, project, configured channel and audience.
It persists the first body and sender for the conversation/key pair, then queues
a bounded, mention-free render through the shared conversation delivery adapter.
A retry repairs an interrupted enqueue using the original body. A Discord reply
to the delivery receipt, or a new message in the channel conversation, becomes
a normal conversation input.

## Side effects and persistence

Writes a `messages` row with `body_kind=conversation_say` and one deduplicated
`outbound_deliveries` row. Earlier inputs keep their state. Returns the delivery
ID and dedup key; delivery follows the normal receipt and retry lifecycle. The
full text persists, while the Discord render is bounded to 1,900 characters.
Database quotas allow 10 new posts per supervisor and 60 per channel in 600
seconds. Replaying an existing key consumes no additional quota.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

`out_of_scope` rejects foreign projects, workers and stale supervisor launches.
`preconditions_unmet` reports disabled conversation support or an unbound outbox.
`visibility_changed` rejects an unauthorized destination or audience.
`conversation_not_open` rejects closed or blocked conversations and unbound
threads. `rate_limited` names the exhausted supervisor or channel quota.
`idempotency_conflict` means another sender already used this key. Use
`aq supervisor-inbox status` and `history` for readiness and conversation IDs;
retry transient enqueue failures with the same key.

## Example step

The supervisor sends the next interview question from a UTF-8 file:

```bash
aq supervisor-inbox say --conversation-id conv-example \
  --file question-two.txt --idempotency-key interview-question-two
```

Keep the key for retries. Use a new key for a distinct question.
